Quarantine expiry is delete_after<=now (quarantine.rs:216) and hold expiry is release_after>now with pruning in mark/sweep runs (quarantine.rs:45-49). findings.evidence: 3 lanes independently (L2 [NEW-L2-01] + L5 [NEW-L5-1] + L10 [NEW-L10-01], deduped): patch_store_usage (lfs.rs:245-266) sums fs::metadata().len() = LOGICAL file size toward the SHARDLINE_LFS_PATCH_TOTAL_MAX_BYTES cap (default 4 TiB). A PATCH with Content-Range bytes 2^40-1-2^40-1/2^40 (total=1 TiB <= MAX_LFS_OBJECT_SIZE, end<total, expected_chunk=1) writes 1 byte at offset 2^40-1 via seek+write_all (lfs.rs:935-943), creating a SPARSE file: logical 1 TiB, real 4 KiB (empirically proven by all 3 lanes, incl. exact harness /tmp/opencode/l10/patch_store_sim.rs). 4 such 1-byte requests exhaust the entire 4 TiB aggregate cap -> every subsequent LFS PATCH from ANY tenant fails 413 LfsPatchStoreFull for up to the 1h TTL, re-refreshable forever at ~16 KiB real disk cost. No admission permit on lfs_patch_object (unlike lfs_put_object). Secondary amplifier: record_lfs_patch_range rewrites the whole .ranges file per PATCH (read-sort-merge-atomic-rewrite), 65k ranges -> CPU/IO amplification loop.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant permanent DoS of the LFS chunked-upload endpoint: 4 requests (16 KiB real disk) pin the aggregate cap at 4 TiB logical, blocking all LFS PATCH uploads server-wide until the TTL sweep, indefinitely refreshable.
findings.reason: 3-lane independent confirmation + empirical proof; F-20 cap accounting unit is wrong (logical vs allocated)
findings.title: LFS PATCH staging cap bypassed via sparse-file logical-size accounting — 4-byte cross-tenant DoS of chunked uploads (F-20 fix defect)

findings.evidence: L2 [NEW-L2-02] (orchestrator-verified in code): PATCH takes store-lock then per-OID lock (lfs.rs:900-925); sweep matches (store->per-OID, lfs.rs:298-301). BUT the promotion success cleanup (lfs.rs:966-972) and error path (lfs.rs:981-987) re-acquire LFS_PATCH_STORE_LOCK while STILL holding the per-OID guard (held from lfs.rs:925 for the whole staged closure) -> per-OID->store inversion. Deadlock: P1 in a long promotion (> TTL) holds per-OID X and blocks on the store lock; P2's sweep holds the store lock and blocks on per-OID X -> permanent deadlock of the whole LFS patch store (all future PATCHes + the startup sweep hang; recovery = restart). The F-20 comment (lfs.rs:200-204, 900-903) claims the opposite order ("no deadlock") — false for the cleanup path. Promotion streams up to 1 TiB (multi-hour on S3 backend at 64 KiB chunk), so promotion-duration > TTL is realistic; the on-PATCH sweep runs on every PATCH.
findings.impact: Permanent deadlock/hang of the LFS chunked-upload subsystem (every PATCH + startup sweep) until process restart, when a long promotion overlaps any sweep.
findings.reason: orchestrator code-verified lock-order inversion in the F-20 fix
findings.title: LFS PATCH store-lock / per-OID-lock order inversion in promotion cleanup — permanent deadlock (F-20 fix defect)

findings.evidence: L9 [NEW-L9-2]: MemoryReconstructionCache::get_or_load waiter branch (cache/src/memory/mod.rs:136-148) awaits notify.notified() with NO timeout; if the loader finishes and fires notify_waiters() before the waiter's notified().await registers, the notification is LOST (tokio Notify keeps no permit for notify_waiters with zero registered waiters — empirically confirmed in sandbox: waiter blocked >2s with the loader having fired) -> the waiter hangs forever with no TTL re-wake. findings.evidence: P5 adv-6 [NEW-P5-L6-1], empirically proven with jsonwebtoken 9.3.1 (pinned): F-38 threads SHARDLINE_AUTH_OIDC_AUDIENCE correctly, but the "unset = permissive" claim is FALSE. verify_jwt_claims builds Validation::new(alg); set_audience called only when self.audience is Some. When unset, validation.aud = None but validate_aud defaults TRUE; jsonwebtoken's validate_aud matches (claims.aud, options.aud) and for (Parsed(_), None) returns Err(InvalidAudience) — presence of aud in the token causes HARD REJECTION when no audience is configured. OIDC Core/RFC 9068 make aud REQUIRED in ID tokens and JWT access tokens (Google/Entra/Auth0/Keycloak/Okta all emit it). The repo's own test signs a token WITHOUT aud, enshrining the wrong belief. Probe: token WITH aud + Validation.aud=None -> Err(InvalidAudience); token WITHOUT aud + None -> Ok; matching aud -> Ok. So every real IdP token -> AuthError::ProviderError -> 401 on every request; the startup warning ("the token aud claim is not validated") is factually wrong.
findings.impact: HIGH (availability): OIDC-configured deployment with unset audience boots successfully then rejects 100% of legitimate tokens — complete silent auth outage; operators told aud is "not validated" get no hint the real behavior is reject-everything.

findings.evidence: P8 L8 [NEW-P8-L8-1], dynamically proven (SQLite probe): the F-75 GC prune orders by created_at_unix_seconds (written by the SERVER wall clock at register_tree_path / refreshed on every touch). The runner's gating rationale ('the prune consults no now, so a jumped clock cannot extend the deletion set') holds only for the GC host's clock; a BACKWARD server step (NTP correction, VM pause/resume, restarted stale-clock server, multi-replica with one replica behind) stamps the newest revision with the SMALLEST created_at, so the prune evicts the NEWEST revision (and cascades its tree entries). Probe: repo at cap 2, rev-1/rev-2 at 1.7e9; server clock 27h behind stamps rev-NEW at 1.6e9; prune(cap=2) -> rev-NEW evicted with its tree. Not self-healing (rebuild never restores tree entries; re-registration blocked at cap via F-89). Also runs on a guard-fired run (prune block not gated by the forward-clock guard), violating F-88's 'fired run deletes nothing'.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: silent deletion of the newest revision's registry row + all its path->file_id tree mappings under a backward server clock + over-cap repo; clients listing that revision see an empty/missing tree; rebuild does not restore; re-registration blocked at cap.

findings.evidence: P8 L9 [NEW-P8-L9-1], dynamically proven (tower oneshot with a dropped future): the cold-miss loading latch (storage/cache, F-90 fix) is removed only on the completion path (load finished or error). findings.evidence: P8 L1 [NEW-P8-L1-1], dynamically proven (real DeleteObjects request against the S3 frontend): the DeleteObjects XML parser never decodes XML entities in <Key> values. A key containing & < > " (e.g. 'a&b') is looked up verbatim, never matches the stored key ('a&b'), and the response emits a FALSE <Deleted> success row for a key that was NOT deleted. Client believes the object is gone while it remains stored (and vice versa: a real delete of 'a&b' reports <Deleted> for 'a&b' — the client's own key). No-op delete with false success acknowledgment.
findings.impact: LOW: false-success delete acknowledgment for entity-encoded keys — client-side data-integrity confusion (object believed deleted but still stored), no cross-tenant exposure, no data loss (the object is NOT actually deleted).
findings.reason: XML entity not decoded in DeleteObjects keys; fix = decode entities or reject with 400
